reasons: No test for this file is visible in the packet.
An empty total returns zero silently, which can hide a missing input.

terms.meaning: A value given as three numbers: low, base and high.
The pessimistic scenario, used to test how bad things could get.
Two values that tend to move together, so their ends should not be combined as if they were unrelated.
Values that do not affect each other.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose of value ranges
sections.what: Explains that every calculated figure keeps a low, base and high value, and that low pairs with low and high pairs with high. It also defines the zero range used as a starting point for totals.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a real downside case has to come from evidence, and a band that is too wide is more honest than one that is falsely narrow.
sections.watch_out: Pairing low with low is right for independent inputs. For linked inputs the band is wider than needed, so readers should not treat band ends as exact.

sections.name: multiply
sections.title: Multiplying two ranges
sections.what: Multiplies two ranges end by end: low by low, base by base and high by high.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file description. The docstring says ends are combined like with like.
sections.watch_out: This function does not check ordering itself. It relies on the Range type to reject results where the ends are out of order, and that check is not shown here.

sections.name: scale
sections.title: Scaling a range by one factor
sections.what: Multiplies all three ends of a range by the same number.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A negative factor flips the low and high ends, so the result may no longer read as low to high.

sections.name: scale_ends
sections.title: Scaling each end by its own factor
sections.what: Multiplies the low, base and high ends by different numbers, for cases where the factor itself changes with the scenario.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a slow ramp pairs with the low case, so the low end needs a different factor from the high end.
sections.watch_out: Passing the factors in the wrong order, for example swapping low and high, silently produces a wrong downside.

sections.name: add
sections.title: Adding two ranges
sections.what: Adds two ranges end by end, low to low, base to base and high to high.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Only meaningful for quantities in the same unit. Nothing here checks that.

sections.name: total
sections.title: Summing a collection of ranges
sections.what: Adds up any number of ranges, starting from a zero range, and returns one range.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file description. Likely reason: it is the common way to total a list of estimates.
sections.watch_out: An empty list returns a zero range without complaint, so a missing input would look like zero benefit.

summary: Provides arithmetic on low, base and high ranges, so that uncertainty carries through every calculated figure.
purpose: Lets calculations combine ranges correctly, so that downside cases come from real inputs rather than a discount applied to the base case.
why: Stated in the docstring: a downside computed from a discount moves when the discount changes, not when the evidence changes. A wider band is more honest than a false claim of precision.
how: Each operation applies the same step to the low, base and high ends separately. The total starts from a zero range and adds each range in turn.
inputs: Range objects, and for scaling, a plain number.
risks: The order of the ends is not checked in this file. An empty total returns zero without complaint. Ranges in different units combine without any warning.
debug: If a downside looks too optimistic, check which ends were passed to each operation. If a total is zero, check that the list of ranges is not empty. Check the Range type for ordering errors.
